description: PBS finds a plan for many agents quickly by searching over priorities between agents. A node of its search tree holds a partial *priority order* (which agents must give way to which) and one path per agent: the cheapest path that avoids the paths of all agents above it. For the earliest conflict between agents `a` and `b`, PBS makes two children, "`a` above `b`" and "`b` above `a`". Each child replans the new lower agent, then every agent below it that now collides with an agent above it. The search is depth-first and tries the cheaper child first; it is neither optimal nor complete, so use it when a good plan is needed fast.

papers.authors: Hang Ma, Daniel Harabor, Peter J. Stuckey, Jiaoyang Li, Sven Koenig
papers.title: Searching with Consistent Prioritization for Multi-Agent Path Finding
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
